footer: Tenable.sc at https://tenable.example.mil. A scan is launched only with tenable_scan_target set and tenable_scan_policy and tenable_scan_repository named; Check launches nothing. The zone of each host: its tenable_zone, else its site (tenable_scan_sites), else the zone whose ranges hold its address, else tenable_scan_zone_default.

sections.text: One scan per zone, from that zone's scanners, with the policy Basic Network Scan into the repository Main. A scan of the same name from an earlier run is updated and launched again, not made twice.
sections.title: Scans

rows: no zone's ranges hold 203.0.113.9 (and no tenable_zone, site or default zone): not scanned
sections.text: Each host's address as the inventory has it, the IP it resolves to from the execution environment, the zone chosen and by which rule - the host's tenable_zone, its site (a group, or the code in its name), its address in the zone's ranges, or the default. A host no rule gives a zone is not scanned (amber).
sections.title: The hosts and their zones

sections.text: From Tenable.sc's analysis of each scan's result: the vulnerabilities by severity on each host scanned. The details are in Tenable.sc (Analysis > Vulnerabilities, the scan's result).
sections.title: Findings by host, the worst first

sections.text: Tenable.sc's scan zones: the IP ranges each covers and the scanners that scan them. A host is scanned from the zone whose ranges hold its address, unless its tenable_zone or its site says otherwise. A scanner not working (amber) is as Tenable.sc's Scanners page shows it.
sections.title: Scan zones and their scanners
